misconceptions.description: A comparison with NULL is thought to be false, though it is unknown, which is why its negation does not select the row either. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: A comparison with null is false

misconceptions.description: A join with an ON condition is thought to return every combination of rows, as if the condition did not filter. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: A join gives every combination

misconceptions.description: A join is thought to return different rows from a loop of queries over the same tables. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: A join returns different rows from a loop

misconceptions.description: A LEFT JOIN is thought to return exactly one row per row of the left table, whatever the number of matches. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: A left join gives one row per left row

misconceptions.description: A LEFT JOIN is thought to return one row per row of the right table only, so the unmatched left rows add nothing. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: A left join gives one row per order

misconceptions.description: A loop of queries is thought to count as one statement. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: A loop of queries is one statement

misconceptions.description: A with conn: block is thought only to commit and never to roll back, so a change before an exception stays. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: A with block never rolls back

misconceptions.description: Statements after a raise are thought still to run. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: Code after a raise still runs

misconceptions.description: COUNT(column) is thought to count the rows with a NULL in the column too, like COUNT(*). Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: Count of a column counts the nulls

misconceptions.description: COUNT(column) is thought to skip zero values, instead of NULL values only. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: Count of a column skips zero

misconceptions.description: COUNT(*) is thought to count only rows with a value and COUNT(column) all rows. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: Count star and count column are swapped

misconceptions.description: COUNT(*) is thought to skip the rows that have a NULL in some column. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: Count star skips rows with a null column

misconceptions.description: A comparison with = NULL is thought to work like IS NULL and to find rows with a missing value. Distinct from sql.null-can-never-be-matched. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: Equals null works like is null

misconceptions.description: A missing value is thought to be impossible to match with any query. Distinct from sql.equals-null-works-like-is-null. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: Null can never be matched

misconceptions.description: NULL is thought to compare equal to zero, so = NULL finds rows with zero. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: Null compares equal to zero

misconceptions.description: After a rollback the last statement of the block is thought to survive. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: Only the last statement survives the rollback

misconceptions.description: Statements in a with conn: block are thought to be queued and run only at the end of the block, instead of at once. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: Statements in a with block are queued until the end

misconceptions.description: The query that fetches the list a loop runs over is thought not to count as a call. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: The first query of a loop is not counted

misconceptions.description: The extra row of a one-to-many join is thought to come from the first left row being counted twice, not from a left row with two matches. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: The first row is counted twice

misconceptions.description: A loop over the parents is thought to make one call per child row instead of one per parent. Editorial hypothesis.
misconceptions.title: The loop makes one call per order
